title: Coordinated Cutover Blueprint: Canary Staging Lanes, Capacity Credits, and Nightly Shadow Runs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
Redwood is preparing a coordinated release across three surfaces (serving runtime, Console, public API) that must preserve customer SLAs while enabling a staged quantization+kernel rollout. Previous rollouts exposed gaps in cross-team signaling (timing of canaries vs console migration), and insufficient capacity hedges for regional spikes.

Objective:
Deliver a repeatable cutover blueprint that defines: canary staging lanes (percentage and cohort definitions), hourly/nightly shadow run schedule to validate traffic and metrics pipelines, a capacity credits matrix (per-region reserve and auto-burst rules), and concrete rollback thresholds/automation for each surface. The blueprint should be consumable by on-call and launch operators during the week-of-cutover.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Define staging lanes and percent rollouts for runtime, console UI changes, and API surface in one coordinated schedule.
- Produce capacity credit policy (how many reserved GPU hours, burst lanes, fallback to lower-cost model variant).
- Nightly shadow run spec: traffic shaping, observability checks, log retention, and canary vs shadow metric comparisons.
- Rollback SLA matrix and automated triggers (latency P99, error rate, end-to-end user flow failures).
- Communication templates for cross-team ops (Slack playbook snippets, PagerDuty escalation verbiage).

Out of scope:
- Implementation of autoscaler changes (ENG will own).
- Model quantization engineering tasks (tracked in runtime initiative).

Success metrics:
- Canary to GA ramp completes without >=2 region SEV level incidents during ramp window.
- Shadow run reveals no more than 5% divergence on core route token costs or 1% divergence on output quality checks across baseline prompts.
- Launch runbook tested in one dry-run rehearsal with on-call and SREs 72 hours prior to launch.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng leads: Daniel Kim (runtime launch lead), Priya Mehta (console release), Luis Ortega (API gateways)
- SRE: Marcus Liu
- Design: Lena Ortiz (console staging UX)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: regional capacity exhaustion during canary ramp. Mitigation: pre-book capacity credits and a documented plan to route to compatible model variants in lower tiers.
- Risk: observability gaps between shadow and canary. Mitigation: mandatory metric parity checklist and alert coverage validation during the rehearsal.

Deliverables:
- Cutover blueprint doc (confluence) with timeline and lane definitions
- Playbook snippets for Slack/PagerDuty and escalation matrix
- Nightly shadow run schedule and verification checklist
- Runbook rehearsal sign-off checklist

Timeline (high level):
- Week 1: Draft blueprint & capacity credit proposal
- Week 2: Review with runtime/console/api leads; iterate on playbook snippets
- Week 3: Rehearsal with SRE + on-call; update doc and lock cadence
- Week 4 (launch window): Execute cutover under runbook
acceptance_criteria: Confluence blueprint document created and reviewed by runtime/console/api leads
Capacity credits reserved and tickets opened with infra (reservation IDs recorded)
Nightly shadow run spec validated in a dry run with metrics collection and pass/fail recorded
Rollback SLA matrix implemented as playbook with automated triggers wired to PagerDuty and runbook
Rehearsal completed with SRE sign-off at least 72 hours before launch
